- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling), model often fails to recognize and undercorrects; adjust downward by 1–2% per day of decline.
- If sentiment history includes a single positive signal (e.g., 0.25), model may overreact; reduce forecast by 2–5% if followed by a downward trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a high, model often fails to anticipate; add a 1–3% buffer to forecast for the next 3–5 days if recent price was above 85.00.
